plan: This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it's incentive compatible. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so shading my bid down only risks losing profitable auctions, while bidding above value risks winning at a loss. Since other bidders are rational, they will also bid their true values. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $23.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy: if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning at a price above your value (loss); if you bid lower, you risk losing an item you'd have profited from. This holds regardless of the other bidders' strategies, since the payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (unless you're the winner). Therefore, I will bid exactly my value, $18, to guarantee optimal expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, truthful bidding is optimal here.
